title: Onboarding QR (pairing an Apple TV or iPad by iPhone)
description: QR code of a device waiting for onboarding (hub mode). Built by the waiting app (Apple TV, iPad, Android TV, Android tablet) from onboard_session, its own pinned TLS fingerprint and its public key. All values are in the URL fragment, so a web server never sees them. The production QR uses the universal link of the brand website (brand.json urls.website, path /pair-tv, Associated Domains; one path for every waiting device: Apple TV, iPad); the development form uses the app scheme. The same path is used by the direct-mode TV sign-in (fragment svc=…, not described here): clients tell them apart by the hub parameter. Contains no secret.

hub.description: Instance id of the hub the waiting device is connected to (onboard_session.hub_id).

n.description: Name of the waiting device for the first screen; percent-encoded in the URI. The confirmation shows the name from onboard_info.

x-client-rules: Only the universal link of the brand website or the app scheme (no aliases), path/host pair-tv; hub mode only when hub, fp, s and k are present.
The confirming device compares fp with the first 32 hex characters of its own pinned fingerprint and refuses on mismatch or when it has no pin.

The confirming device shows the fingerprint (first 16 hex characters in groups of 4) like the waiting device, the name, the area choice and the rights from onboard_info, and sends nothing before the user confirms (onboard_lookup is a read).
The waiting device offers onboarding only when it connected over TLS pinned to the fingerprint from Bonjour; it shows the same short fingerprint next to the QR code.
